text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Chemicals concern Akzo Nobel's Q2 net profit up 25 pct to Dfl 459 million due to coatings division. (p1)
- Cool reaction of investors to paper and office equipment producer KNP BT's second quarter figures. (p1)
- ABN Amro fails to get into consortium that leads re-issue of Lufthansa shares. (p1)
- Dairy group Campina expands its Polish activities. (p4)
- Number of private persons who were declared bankrupt jumps 24 pct in first six months of 1997. (p5) DE VOLKSKRANT
- The number of dairy cows in the Netherlands has decreased by nearly 40 pct since introduction of milk quota. (p2)
- ABN Amro Hoare Govett Asia takes 35 pct stake in Thai Merchant bank and broker Asia Securities Trading. (p11)
- Insurer Interpolis first half 1997 net profits grew by nine percent to Dfl 118 million. (p11) DE TELEGRAAF
- KNP BT expects a solution for ailing paper unit KNP Leykam soon. (p19)
- Candy maker Klene books seven percent higher net profit in first six months of 1997 on 1.2 pct turnover growth. (p21) ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Food and detergent giant Unilever is to shut its Unifrost ice cream plant near Vienna, Austria next spring. (p11)
